issues.sym: Rough idle, stalling, misfires, hard or no starting, or random electrical faults that come and go; the wire coating near the engine looks cracked or flakes off when touched.
issues.why: Mercedes used an eco-friendly wire coating in this era that breaks down with engine heat and age, leaving bare wires that can short against each other.
issues.next: Have the engine harness inspected. If the insulation is cracking, replace the harness rather than patching it, since shorted wires can damage control units or start a fire.

issues.sym: Oil seeping down the back or side of the engine, a burning oil smell after driving, and in later stages coolant loss or overheating.
issues.why: The head gasket on these engines tends to start weeping oil with age and high mileage, usually at the rear of the cylinder head first.
issues.next: Have the leak traced while it is still small. Watch the temperature gauge and coolant level, and stop driving if the engine starts to overheat.

issues.t: Body rust and broken front spring perches
issues.sym: Rust bubbles on doors, wheel arches and around trim, or a clunk and a sagging front corner if a spring breaks or its mount rusts through.
issues.why: Paint and corrosion protection on this generation were weak, and road salt attacks the front spring mounts and coil springs.
issues.next: Have the underbody and front spring mounts checked, especially in salt-belt areas. A broken spring or rusted-through mount should be fixed before regular driving.

issues.t: Sunroof glass panel can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some owners notice wind noise or a panel that feels loose; in rare cases the glass can separate from the car while driving.
issues.why: The adhesive holding the sliding sunroof glass to its frame can weaken with age. Mercedes-Benz recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the free sunroof repair done at a dealer. Keep the sunroof closed until it is fixed.

issues.t: Radiator leaks coolant into the transmission
issues.sym: Harsh or erratic shifting, a droning noise at low engine speeds, slipping, or milky pink transmission fluid.
issues.why: Early radiators have a built-in transmission fluid cooler whose internal seal can fail, letting engine coolant mix into the automatic transmission fluid and damage it.
issues.next: If shifting suddenly turns harsh, stop driving and have the transmission fluid checked for coolant. Many owners replace the original radiator early as prevention.

issues.t: Timing chain stretch on the supercharged 4-cylinder
issues.sym: A rattle for a few seconds after a cold start, a check engine light with camshaft timing codes, or rough running.
issues.why: The timing chain and its tensioner on this engine can wear and stretch early. If it jumps a tooth, the valves can hit the pistons.
issues.next: Do not ignore a cold-start rattle. Have the chain stretch and timing checked soon, before it can skip and wreck the engine.

issues.t: Oil wicking from camshaft solenoids into the wiring
issues.sym: Check engine light, oxygen sensor or airflow sensor faults, poor running, and oil found inside electrical plugs at the front of the engine.
issues.why: Oil seeps past the seals of the camshaft timing solenoids and travels inside the wiring toward sensors and even the engine computer.
issues.next: Replace the leaking solenoids and clean or repair the affected wiring. Fixing it early keeps oil from reaching the engine computer.

issues.t: Balance shaft or idler gear wear on the V6
issues.sym: Check engine light with camshaft and crankshaft correlation codes, rough running or hesitation, and sometimes a rattle from the front of the engine.
issues.why: A timing drive gear on earlier M272 V6 engines was made from metal that wears too quickly, letting the timing drift out of spec. Later engines got an improved gear.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the timing checked by a Mercedes specialist. The repair is major, so get it diagnosed before the timing chain jumps.

issues.sym: Harsh or delayed shifts, the transmission stuck in one gear (limp mode), or a transmission warning on the dash.
issues.why: The electronic conductor plate inside the 7G-Tronic transmission, which carries the speed sensors, can fail and send the control unit bad information.
issues.next: Have the transmission scanned for speed-sensor faults. Replacing the conductor plate usually restores normal shifting without a full rebuild.

issues.sym: The key turns but nothing happens, the steering wheel stays locked, or the car starts only some of the time.
issues.why: The electronic steering lock module can fail internally, so the car never confirms the steering is unlocked and refuses to start.
issues.next: Try the spare key first to rule out a key problem. If it still will not start, the steering lock module needs replacing and coding.

issues.t: Tail lights dim or fail from a poor ground (recall)
issues.sym: Bulb-out warnings, dim or flickering tail and brake lights, or lights that work only some of the time.
issues.why: A poor ground connection in the tail lamp wiring causes weak contact, which led to a recall.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done at a dealer. Working brake lights matter for safety.

issues.t: Timing chain and camshaft adjuster rattle on the turbo 4-cylinder
issues.sym: A loud rattle for a few seconds after a cold start, a check engine light with camshaft timing codes, or rough idle.
issues.why: The camshaft adjusters and timing chain parts on this engine can wear, letting the chain run loose at startup and the timing drift.
issues.next: Have the timing components checked soon after the rattle or codes appear. Letting it go can lead to a skipped chain and serious engine damage.

issues.t: Starter circuit current limiter can overheat (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning in normal use. The risk shows up when the engine is cranked over and over without starting, which can overheat a part in the starter circuit.
issues.why: If the starter is strained by repeated cranking, a current limiter in its circuit can overheat and create a fire risk. The recall fix adds an extra fuse.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and get the free repair. Until then, if the engine will not start, do not keep cranking it, and stop if you smell burning wiring.

issues.t: Camshaft adjuster wear and oil in the engine wiring
issues.sym: Check engine light with camshaft timing codes, a short rattle at cold start, or oil found in electrical connectors on top of the engine.
issues.why: The intake camshaft adjuster can wear, and oil can seep past the camshaft solenoid seals and travel along the wiring harness.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the camshaft solenoids and connectors checked for oil. Replace leaking parts early so oil does not reach other sensors or modules.

issues.t: Fuel pump can shut down while driving (recall)
issues.sym: Sudden stalling or loss of power while driving, or hard starting.
issues.why: The fuel pump in the tank may stop working, cutting fuel to the engine. Mercedes-Benz recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done right away. If the car stalls, get it safely off the road and have it towed.

issues.sym: Often no warning before failure; a warning message may appear in the instrument cluster once the connection overheats.
issues.why: Some ground bolts for the 12-volt and 48-volt systems were not tightened to spec at the factory. The loose joint can heat up and create a fire risk.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls and have the dealer inspect and tighten the connections for free. Do not ignore an electrical warning message.
